newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON TUNES UP FOR MATCH RACE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON TUNES UP FOR MATCH RACE.

text.p: Michael Johnson, in his final tuneup for next Sunday's match race with Canada's Donovan Bailey, ran a relaxed 200 meters to highlight the 23rd annual Prefontaine Classic at Hayward Field Sunday.

In contrast with his world record 19.32 seconds, Johnson's winning time of 20.17 seconds looked rather leisurely. But a sold-out crowd of 13,856 cheered his performance in the last event of the meeting.

"It's good to be appreciated," Johnson said. "This is a great place to run, in front of people who like track and field. Conditions were good for me. It wasn't too cold. This was all I needed to do. I just needed to get a race in."

Americans Jon Drummond (20.46), Maurice Greene and Olympic high hurdles champion Allen Johnson (20.51) followed Johnson across the finish line. Earlier, Drummond was third in the 100 (10.16) while Allen Johnson was upset in the 110 hurdles by Olympic silver medallist Mark Crear, 13.18 to 13.42.
Johnson said he expects to win his 150-meter match race with Bailey at Toronto's SkyDome. Drummond explained why he agrees with his U.S. teammate.
"The advantage in the 150 meters is the turn," Drummond said. "If you run 150 on a straight, Donovan Bailey has the advantage. But if you run it on a turn, Michael Johnson has the advantage."

The best mark in the meet was produced by Maria Mutola of Mozambique in the women's 800 meters. Running in front of her hometown fans, she ran the fastest time in the world this year, 1 minute 57.57 seconds, to hold off American Jearl Miles in 1:57.98.

"It helped me a lot," Mutola said of the enthusiastic crowd. "They give all the support I need. It's beautiful to run here. I hope to run faster. I have a dream to get the world record. It's not easy but I keep dreaming."
American athletes were predominant in the only IAAF Grand Prix meeting in the United States but the streamlined, two-hour event also featured a foreign presence.

Ireland's Sonia O'Sullivan defeated American Suzy Hamilton in the 1,500 by running 4:06.35. Valentina Fedyushi of Ukraine led the shot put at 18.86 until the last throw of the competition, when American Connie Price-Smith reached 19.19.
Britain's Mark Richardson upset an American-dominated field to win the 400 in 45.30, defeating Deon Minor, Lamont Smith, Anthuan Maybank and Calvin Harrison in the process.
Hometown favourite Mary Slaney, 38, pulled out of the meet with a leg injury. So did Carl Lewis, who felt a tight Achilles tendon while warming up for the 100 and scratched from the race.
"The problem has been pushing out of the blocks," Lewis said. "It's painful. I think in a couple weeks I'll be all right."
